name: Tabs
purpose: Switches between related views of the same context (Overview / Standings / Fixtures) without leaving the page.

props.name: items
props.type: Array<{ id: string; label: ReactNode; content: ReactNode; icon?: IconName; badge?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }>

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Uncontrolled initial tab (defaults to first enabled).

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the tab list when no visible heading labels it.

props.name: activation
props.description: automatic selects on arrow; manual requires Enter/Space (use for slow panels).

props.name: variant
props.description: Underline indicator or segmented control look.

props.name: fitted
props.description: Tabs share the full width equally (2–4 tabs on mobile).

states.name: selected
states.description: Brand text, semibold, 3px indicator bar (line) or raised pill (contained).

states.name: disabled
states.description: Disabled text, skipped by arrow keys.

keyboard.action: Focus the selected tab, then into the panel.

screenReader: Tabs announced as '<label>, tab, selected, n of m'.
Panels are labelled by their tab.
accessibility.focus: Roving tabindex: only the selected tab is in the tab order. Panels are focusable so their content is reachable.
notes: Selected state uses an indicator and weight, not color alone.

variants.name: contained
variants.useWhen: Switching views in a card or toolbar (List / Grid / Bracket).

do: Keep labels to one or two words.
Use when users don't need to compare content across tabs.
dont: Don't use Tabs for sequential steps — use a stepper / wizard.
Don't use Tabs for top-level site navigation — use links.
Don't exceed ~6 tabs; consider a Select on mobile.

example.web:
<Tabs
  aria-label="Tournament"
  items={[
    { id: 'overview', label: 'Overview', content: <Overview /> },
    { id: 'standings', label: 'Standings', content: <Standings /> },
    { id: 'disputes', label: 'Disputes', badge: 3, content: <Disputes /> },
  ]}
/>
